peerMapping.justification: Three-run Kimi K3 consensus selected only the displayed peers: NVDA 33.2% with 3/3 replicate support; AMD 21.7% with 3/3 replicate support; MU 17.3% with 3/3 replicate support; INTC 11.6% with 3/3 replicate support; XYZ100 9.0% with 2/3 replicate support; MRVL 7.2% with 2/3 replicate support. Individual rationales state each economic relationship.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: Most direct single-name comparator: NVIDIA is a leading semiconductor designer for AI accelerators and is often a dominant driver of US semiconductor index returns.

peers.name: Advanced Micro Devices
peers.reason: AMD is a top-tier constituent of the same semiconductor index and competes directly with NVIDIA in GPUs and AI accelerators, so its returns co-move tightly with the basket SOXL tracks. It is a direct underlying exposure rather than a proxy, which is why it ranks ahead of remote factor analogies.

peers.name: Micron Technology
peers.reason: Micron sells memory and storage chips, so its revenue and margins move with the same semiconductor pricing and capital-spending cycle.

peers.name: Intel
peers.reason: Intel adds logic-chip design and manufacturing exposure; it is less pure than the AI leaders but still a core US semiconductor return driver.

peers.name: Nasdaq-100
peers.reason: The Nasdaq-100 is the dominant systematic index for mega-cap technology and is heavily semiconductor-weighted, so it captures the broad tech beta component of SOXL's daily leveraged moves; it also serves as the primary hedge and has the deepest 24-hour perp liquidity in the basket at 112.294 USD millions.

peers.name: Marvell Technology
peers.reason: Marvell is a constituent of the same index with data-center networking and custom-silicon exposure tied to the same AI infrastructure spending cycle as the larger chip names.

primary_index_hedge.name: Nasdaq-100
primary_index_hedge.reason: Nasdaq-100 is the closest broad systematic hedge in the universe for a leveraged semiconductor equity product: it absorbs generic US large-cap growth and risk-on or risk-off beta without pretending to be the semiconductor cycle itself.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; the basket begins with the first available selected peer, unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted, and remaining weights are renormalized; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current Hyperliquid native or TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's matching-venue perp close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights are renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

underlierSelection.method: highest summed live contract volume; open interest and contract count break ties

model.name: ATM-straddle-implied lognormal distribution
model.description: Each target uses the nearest paired liquid ATM call and put. Their combined ask implies the expiration distribution shown on the chart.
model.measure: option-implied, not a historical or physical forecast
